answer: An agent marketplace requires each identity to lock a $100 bond for 30 days before bidding on work, whether monitoring tundra sensors, scheduling harbor cranes, or watering a garden. The same bond cannot back multiple identities, so creating 1,000 eligible agents ties up $100,000 for a month. Fake names remain cheap, but gaining marketplace access at scale requires capital that the attacker cannot spend elsewhere during the lock.
